newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain arrests four for deadly arson attack.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain arrests four for deadly arson attack.

text.p: Bahrain on Sunday arrested four suspects after an arson attack which killed a Bangladeshi worker.
"A group of saboteurs who set fire to a cold store in Sitra in which an Asian worker died and another was seriously injured have been arrested," the official Gulf News Agency said.
A government official told Reuters the group comprised four Bahrainis who were arrested on Sunday after the Saturday night attack.
The deadly attack was the latest in a series of incidents that have hit the island, the Gulf's main financial and banking centre and headquarters for the United States Fifth Fleet.
"A group of people stormed the store and set it ablaze. Two Asians were inside the store which was completely gutted," the agency said earlier on Sunday.
Seven Bangladeshi workers died when suspected arsonists set a restaurant ablaze in Sitra, linked with the capital Manama by a three km (1.8 miles) causeway, in March 1996.
Four Indians died from smoke inhalation and a fifth was critically injured after fire gutted a shop in Manama in June.

A power generator blew up at a luxury hotel in Manama on Saturday, causing a fire but there were no reports of damage or casualties, officials said. The previous day three fires broke out in Muharraq, linked with Manama by another causeway, causing damage but there were no reports of casualties.

On Tuesday, an explosion hit a hotel in central Manama and witnesses said part of the roof of the hotel's nightclub had collapsed. A government official said initial reports indicated that a gas leak caused the blast.
A series of arson attacks in early June were described by a government official as "continued acts of terrorism".

Members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged sporadic protests, bombings and arson attacks since December 1994 to press the Sunni-led government to introduce economic and political reforms.
Among the victims of the attacks have been members of Bahrain's Asian community, who some Bahrainis believe are taking away jobs.
